newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan April overall oil demand falls 5.4 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Japan April overall oil demand falls 5.4 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Overall Japanese oil demand fell by 5.4 percent in April from the same month a year earlier to 19.81 million kilolitres (4.15 million barrels-per-day), trade ministry statistics showed on Monday.
Overall oil demand groups domestic sales of petroleum products with crude oil used for direct burning in electricity generation, petrochemical production, fertiliser production, and other uses.

Crude oil used for direct burning by electric utilities in April fell by 44.1 percent from a year earlier to 534,000 kl (112,000 bpd), Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) statistics showed.

The drop reflects a warmer April this year compared with the same month last year as well as a longer term MITI initiative to reduce dependence on thermal power generation involving the burning of crude and fuel oil.
Domestic product sales were also hit by the warmer weather, with a 21.5 percent fall in kerosene demand outweighing small gains in gasoline and naphtha sales.
Kerosene is used for home heating in Japan.
Crude oil for petrochemical use in April was 29 percent higher at 220,550 kl (46,240 bpd) than the same month a year earlier.
